nodes.content: Develop a classifier robust to instance-dependent label noise without discarding difficult examples from underrepresented groups.
requirements: Under 30% label corruption, improve worst-group accuracy by five percentage points over empirical risk minimization.
Establish identifiability conditions without requiring clean labels or known group membership during training.

nodes.content: Train TriView-CVaR using three conditionally independent annotators with full-rank, diagonally dominant noise channels and feature-cluster CVaR retaining all examples.
Under which conditions can TriView-CVaR identify clean-label probabilities from feature-dependent noisy annotators without verified labels or group membership?
Three conditionally independent annotators with full-rank, diagonally dominant noise matrices uniquely identify clean-label posteriors wherever every class has positive probability.
Prove pointwise Kruskal uniqueness with positive class priors and diagonal-dominance permutation anchoring; construct rank-deficient counterexamples.
Pointwise three-view Kruskal proof establishes unique clean-label posteriors for K≥2 with positive priors and full-rank channels; diagonal dominance anchors classes.
Adopt three-view posterior correction with diagonal-dominance anchoring, since the uniqueness proof requires neither clean labels nor observed groups.
Implement adopted three-view correction with full-sample feature-cluster CVaR; test ≥5-point worst-group accuracy gains over ERM at 25% corruption.
Benchmark TriView-CVaR against ERM on Waterbirds with three conditionally independent annotators, 25% instance-dependent flips, and evaluation-only groups.
Waterbirds-25 benchmark report contains per-group accuracies, annotator confusion estimates, corruption seeds, and retained-example counts for TriView-CVaR and ERM.
Audit Waterbirds-25 report across five seeds for ≥5-point worst-group accuracy gains over ERM and complete minority-cluster retention.
Across five Waterbirds-25 seeds, TriView-CVaR reached 65% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 63%, missing the five-point target despite full retention.
TriView-SoftDRO replaces feature-cluster CVaR with overlapping-cluster DRO on three-view posteriors and strictly positive weights for every sample.
At 25% corruption, group-blind overlapping clusters capture minority errors, enabling SoftDRO to exceed ERM worst-group accuracy by ≥5 points.
Using Waterbirds-25 report seeds, test whether TriView-SoftDRO reaches ≥68% worst-group accuracy across five seeds without zero-weight examples.
Across five Waterbirds-25 seeds, TriView-SoftDRO achieved 66% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 63%; all sample weights remained positive.
Adding posterior-gradient disagreement to SoftDRO clusters should reach ≥68% Waterbirds-25 worst-group accuracy while keeping every sample weighted.
Rerun Waterbirds-25’s five report seeds with posterior-gradient-disagreement clusters; compare worst-group accuracy against 68% and verify positive sample weights.
Five-seed Waterbirds-25 mean worst-group accuracy was 67% with gradient-disagreement clusters, below 68%; every training sample retained positive weight.
Using Waterbirds-25 report seeds, sweep gradient-disagreement cluster overlap and DRO temperature; test ≥68% worst-group accuracy and positive weights.
At 40% cluster overlap and 0.2 DRO temperature, Waterbirds-25 five-seed worst-group accuracy reached 69% versus ERM’s 63%; weights remained positive.
Unlike untuned gradient clusters, fixed 40%-overlap, 0.2-temperature SoftDRO should reach ≥68% worst-group accuracy on held-out Waterbirds-25 seeds, retaining all examples.
Using Waterbirds-25 report protocol, evaluate fixed 40%-overlap, 0.2-temperature SoftDRO on five new seeds against ERM, auditing worst-group accuracy and retention.
Five held-out Waterbirds-25 seeds yielded 69% mean worst-group accuracy for fixed SoftDRO versus ERM’s 63%, with all examples weighted.
TriView-CalDRO augments three-view posterior correction with uncertainty-calibrated gradient clusters and adaptive DRO temperature, enforcing positive weights without group labels.
How can posterior uncertainty calibrate gradient-cluster membership and DRO temperature without downweighting genuinely hard minority examples?
Entropy-binned posterior-gradient disagreement distinguishes noise from hard examples; variance-scaled temperature retains ≥0.2×uniform weights and ≥68% Waterbirds-25 worst-group accuracy.
On five unseen Waterbirds-25 seeds, test entropy-binned gradients and variance-scaled temperature for noise–hard separation, ≥68% worst-group accuracy, and ≥0.2×uniform weights.
On five unseen Waterbirds-25 seeds, CalDRO scored 67% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 63%; minimum weight was 0.23×uniform.
TriView-RecallDRO uses identifiable three-annotator posteriors and overlapping latent error clusters, imposing cluster recall floors with strictly positive example weights.
Estimate three-view posteriors, enforce latent-cluster recall floors without training groups, then test ≥68% Waterbirds-25 worst-group accuracy with full retention.
Implement RecallDRO’s differentiable 70% posterior-weighted recall floor for overlapping error clusters, retaining a 0.2×uniform example-weight minimum.
RecallDRO-v1 training code implements three-view posterior estimation, overlapping error-cluster recall constraints, and a 0.2×uniform weight floor.
Benchmark RecallDRO-v1 on five unseen Waterbirds-25 seeds against ERM, measuring worst-group accuracy, latent-cluster recall, and minimum example weight.
Across five unseen Waterbirds-25 seeds, RecallDRO-v1 reached 70% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 63%, with ≥70% cluster recall and ≥0.2×uniform weights.
Test RecallDRO-v1 against ERM on CelebA at 29% instance-dependent corruption, measuring worst-group accuracy and retention with evaluation-only groups.
On CelebA-29, RecallDRO-v1 achieved 72% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 69%, missing the five-point target despite full retention.
Defer RecallDRO-v1 as a general solution: Waterbirds-25 clears the target, but CelebA-29 misses it by two points.
TriView-LocalRecallDRO splits overlapping error clusters into feature neighborhoods, enforcing three-view posterior-recall floors and positive weights without training groups.
Can feature-local recall floors close CelebA-29’s two-point target gap without amplifying noisy outliers or downweighting hard examples?
Building on fixed-overlap SoftDRO, local recall floors yield ≥74% CelebA-29 worst-group accuracy, noisy-outlier weights ≤2×uniform, and minimum weights ≥0.2×uniform.
Use Waterbirds-25 report’s corruption protocol to test LocalRecallDRO on CelebA-29: ≥74% worst-group accuracy, outlier weights ≤2×uniform, minimum ≥0.2×uniform.
On CelebA-29, LocalRecallDRO reached 75% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 69%; outlier weights peaked at 1.8×uniform, minimum 0.22×uniform.
Using Waterbirds-25 report seeds, compare LocalRecallDRO and ERM at 25% corruption; audit worst-group accuracy, outlier weights, and full retention.
Waterbirds-25 weight audit exposed a normalization error; rechecking CelebA-29 raised measured outlier weights from 1.8× to 2.7×uniform.
Capping all sample weights at 2×uniform in fixed-overlap LocalRecallDRO should retain ≥74% CelebA-29 worst-group accuracy and ≥0.2×uniform minima.
Using Waterbirds-25 protocol, test 2×uniform-capped LocalRecallDRO on five CelebA-29 seeds for ≥74% worst-group accuracy and ≥0.2×uniform minimum weights.
Five CelebA-29 seeds gave capped LocalRecallDRO 74% mean worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 69%, with weights spanning 0.21–2.0×uniform.
Adopt corrected, 2×uniform-capped LocalRecallDRO for CelebA-29: it preserves a five-point gain while addressing mismeasured outlier weights.
Freeze capped LocalRecallDRO; evaluate new Waterbirds-25/CelebA-29 seeds for ≥5-point worst-group gains, group-blind training, positive weights, and channel rank.
Run frozen capped LocalRecallDRO on five fresh Waterbirds-25/CelebA-29 seeds each; audit worst-group gains, channel rank, group-blind training, and weights.
LocalRecallDRO-v2 audit report records fresh-seed group accuracies, annotator channel singular values, training-feature inventory, and normalized example-weight ranges.
Audit LocalRecallDRO-v2 report for ≥5-point gains on both datasets, CelebA-29 ≥74%, full-rank channels, group-blind training, and 0.2–2×uniform weights.
Fresh-seed Waterbirds-25/CelebA-29 worst-group accuracies were 69%/75% versus ERM’s 63%/69%; channels were full-rank, training group-blind, weights 0.21–2×uniform.
Bootstrap LocalRecallDRO-v2’s CelebA-29 audit seeds to assess uncertainty around ≥74% worst-group accuracy and the ≥0.2×uniform weight floor.
Among 500 CelebA-29 bootstrap refits, 18% breached the 0.2×uniform weight floor after normalization; minimum observed weight was 0.18×uniform.
Project fixed-overlap LocalRecallDRO weights onto the normalized [0.2,2]×uniform simplex; expect ≥74% CelebA-29 worst-group accuracy across bootstrap refits.
Using Waterbirds-25 report’s corruption protocol, run 500 projected-weight CelebA-29 bootstrap refits; audit ≥74% worst-group accuracy and [0.2,2]×uniform weights.
Across 500 CelebA-29 bootstrap refits, projected LocalRecallDRO achieved ≥74% worst-group accuracy; every normalized weight stayed within [0.2,2]×uniform.
Adopt simplex-projected LocalRecallDRO: capped versions gained five–six points but breached bootstrap weight floors; projection retained ≥74% CelebA-29 accuracy.
Replace capped weights with [0.2,2]×uniform simplex projection; test ≥5-point gains on fresh Waterbirds-25/CelebA-29 seeds, full-rank channels, and group-blind training.
Using LocalRecallDRO-v2 audit report’s protocol, rerun projected LocalRecallDRO on five fresh Waterbirds-25/CelebA-29 seeds each; check gains, rank, weights, and group-blinding.
LocalRecallDRO-v3 audit report replaces capped-weight results with fresh-seed projected-weight accuracies, channel ranks, group-blinding checks, and normalized-weight ranges.
Audit LocalRecallDRO-v3 for ≥5-point worst-group gains on both datasets, CelebA-29 ≥74%, full-rank channels, group-blinding, and [0.2,2]×uniform weights.
Fresh-seed projected LocalRecallDRO scored 70%/74% worst-group accuracy versus ERM’s 63%/69% on Waterbirds-25/CelebA-29; full-rank channels, group-blind training, [0.2,2]×uniform weights.
Adopt projected LocalRecallDRO-v3: seven/five-point worst-group gains meet both benchmarks, and guaranteed weight bounds eliminate capped-model bootstrap breaches.
